key_value_text.value: Zenith-angle-dependent deficit of muon neutrinos inconsistent with expectations for no oscillation; data consistent with two-flavour nu_mu <-> nu_tau oscillation.

name: Super-Kamiokande evidence for atmospheric neutrino oscillation

summary.plain: In 1998, Super-Kamiokande found a zenith-angle-dependent deficit of atmospheric muon neutrinos: fewer arrived from the far side of the Earth than expected. The collaboration's paper is titled 'Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos'; its history page calls this compelling evidence for neutrino oscillations, overturning the assumption that neutrinos are massless.
summary.technical: 33.0 kiloton-year (535-day) exposure; a zenith-angle-dependent muon-neutrino deficit inconsistent with expectations based on calculations of the atmospheric neutrino flux, consistent with two-flavour νμ↔ντ oscillation. The paper's title is 'Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos'.

title: Evidence for oscillation of atmospheric neutrinos
why_it_matters: The Super-Kamiokande history page says the collaboration discovered compelling evidence of neutrino oscillations, overturning the long-held assumption that neutrinos are massless, and that this discovery eventually led to Kamioka's second Nobel Prize in Physics.
